findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - a client configures separate full and pull-request test commands.
The Done-when item is: “A client with one test group gets one tests job that also does the docs-only check, and a test command that cannot be split runs in one group instead of repeating.” Group selection examines only `test` (`src/forge/repo.py:691`), but the PR command uses `fast_test` when set (`src/forge/review.py:369`). With three groups, a sharded `test` and unsharded `fast_test` therefore still run the same PR tests three times. Conversely, an unsharded `test` and sharded `fast_test` reduce the PR to one group, losing its configured parallelism.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Gate
Case: normal use - running the nightly or release full suite.
The new single-group workflow removes the matrix and two jobs, but existing tests still require the old shape. `tests/test_groups_pytest.py:145` expects the removed one-group matrix expression, and `tests/test_ci_runner_selection.py:31` expects six runner entries where the migrated workflow now has four. Those assertions will fail and prevent a green full-suite result; the first failure also prevents the rest of its multi-group coverage from running.
findings.title: Gate: existing full-suite workflow tests

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a client uses `fast_test` for pull-request checks.
The named single-group proof removes `fast_test` before configuring the client, and `tests/test_unsplit_groups_warning.py:39` does the same. The existing `tests/test_groups_any_runner.py:101` case supplies group variables manually without checking the generated workflow after setting `fast_test`. The proofs therefore pass when the actual PR command is repeated across groups or its valid sharding is collapsed.
findings.title: Gate: fast_test group-selection proof

stop.reason: Harm 3 findings: one more round by the standing rule

why: A client pull request with one test group starts three small gate jobs around its test job, and a hand-set group count without a shard flag repeats the same tests in every group
